title: red-pipeline, the intake ci detector and ql_deliver read pipelines through bl_forge with the configured project
goal: bl_intake.latest_pipeline, its job traces and ql_deliver.forge_list, the job-list read and the CI check of querylog apply read the forge through bl_forge, with the forge and forge_project settings (ql_deliver and bl_intake no longer re-derive the project from the URL); neither module runs glab or gh itself; a project with no setting reads the remote's URL as before

run: import sys; sys.exit(1 if any('"glab"' in open(f, encoding='utf-8').read() for f in ('_tools/bl_intake.py', '_tools/ql_deliver.py')) else 0)

gates.question: Which forge does a read by a remote's url (the intake CI detector, the delivery CI check) use when the forge setting is its default gitlab and the url names github.com?
options: the url's forge (github.com is GitHub, read through gh), as the tools read it before the settings, while the root-based land and merge reads keep refusing that pair
refuse it as the root-based reads do (Refused, no pipeline read, a note)
gates.recommendation: the url's forge (github.com is GitHub, read through gh), as the tools read it before the settings, while the root-based land and merge reads keep refusing that pair
gates.answer: the url's forge (github.com is GitHub, read through gh), as the tools read it before the settings, while the root-based land and merge reads keep refusing that pair

gates.question: Does the delivery CI check keep the separate auth status call before its pipeline read, or read the pipeline directly through bl_forge and take a failed read as the skip?
options: read directly: one call fewer, and the skip note is the CLI's own failure line
keep a bl_forge signed-in verb and the glab or gh auth status call first, as forge_list does for the open conflict merge requests
gates.recommendation: read directly: one call fewer, and the skip note is the CLI's own failure line
gates.answer: read directly: one call fewer, and the skip note is the CLI's own failure line
